quick: Dogs and cats 90 days or older from the US

ISO 11784/11785 microchip, current rabies vaccination given before arrival, and a rabies-neutralizing antibody (FAVN) result of 0.5 IU/ml or more from an internationally approved lab, with the blood drawn within 24 months. If everything checks out, the pet can be released on the day of arrival.

A health certificate issued by a USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 30 days of export. The vet can submit it through VEHCS, but APHIS must ink-sign and emboss it, and the original must travel with your pet.
No rabies vaccination or antibody test needed, but they still need an ISO microchip and a certificate showing the chip number and birth date.
Only needed when you bring 10 or more dogs and/or cats: send APQA an advance notification and get approval for a quarantine facility first.

No microchip, a chip number that doesn't match, no antibody test or a result under 0.5 IU/ml: the pet is held in quarantine at your expense (APQA says 10 days on average, sometimes longer). With no health certificate, the pet is sent back at your cost.

South Korea is not on the CDC high-risk list for dog rabies, so a dog that was only in low-risk countries in the past 6 months needs the free CDC Dog Import Form receipt, a microchip, a healthy look and an age of 6 months or more.

rules.rule: Required at every age. The chip must meet ISO 11784/11785 (implanted or necklace type). With any other chip, bring your own scanner. The chip number must match the health certificate.
Must be current and given before arrival in Korea. Not required for pets under 90 days old.

Required for pets 90 days or older from countries that are not rabies-free; APHIS lists it as required for US dogs and cats. Done by an internationally approved lab or the exporting country's authority; result 0.5 IU/ml or more; valid for 24 months from the blood draw. Pets from areas on APQA's rabies-free list are exempt, so if you fly from Hawaii or Guam, check that list with APQA. The APQA and APHIS pages we checked don't list a waiting period after the draw; confirm with APQA.

rules.case: Test or chip done after arrival
rules.rule: If the antibody test or microchip can't be done before you fly (or the test is more than 24 months old), it can be done after arrival in Korea, but the pet will likely be held in quarantine at your expense until it is complete, and a valid USDA-endorsed certificate is still required.

Issued by a USDA-accredited vet (electronic signature accepted) and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 30 days of export. Submission can be via VEHCS; APHIS ink-signs and embosses the certificate, and the endorsed original must accompany the pet. You can have it returned by mail with a prepaid label.
Date of birth, microchip number, the antibody test result, test date and lab, the issuing agency, issue date, and the issuer's name and signature, plus a statement that the animal is healthy.
Required only for 10 or more dogs and/or cats: submit an advance notification form to APQA and get prior approval to use an animal quarantine facility.
Tick the animal box on the customs declaration and present it, with the quarantine certificate from the departure country, to the quarantine officer.
Once the documents are verified and a clinical exam at the port of entry confirms the pet is healthy, it may be released on the day of arrival.

Extended quarantine at your expense until the chip is implanted or the antibody titer reaches 0.5 IU/ml (APQA says 10 days on average, longer in some cases). Without a health certificate, the pet is returned to the exporting country at your cost.
If you travel under official orders, APHIS points to the US Army Medical Department Korea site for extra information.

South Korea is not on the CDC list of high-risk countries for dog rabies (North Korea is). A dog that was only in rabies-free or low-risk countries in the past 6 months needs the free CDC Dog Import Form receipt, must look healthy, be 6 months or older and have a microchip.
No federal rabies proof or USDA health requirements for pet cats; they must look healthy. State, airline, Hawaii and Guam rules still apply.

fees.item: USDA APHIS endorsement, 1-2 lab tests on the certificate
fees.amount: $160 for one pet; +$10 for each extra pet on the same certificate. Check with APHIS which tier your certificate falls in.
Set by the lab and your vet; check with the lab.

fees.item: Quarantine in Korea if requirements aren't met
fees.amount: Paid by the owner; APQA's English page gives no amount. Check with APQA.

fees.item: CDC Dog Import Form (return to the US)

offices.office: APQA, Incheon International Airport (pets shipped as cargo)

intro: Most of Korea's public transport takes small pets in a closed carrier, and nothing else. On trains, subways and buses the usual limit is 10 kg (22 lb) for pet and carrier together, and the pet must stay inside, out of sight. A large dog is harder: a pet taxi, a ferry pet room or driving are usually the options.
Rules come from each operator. Most official pages are in Korean; we summarize them in English.

cards.sub: KTX, ITX, Mugunghwa and other Korail services
cards.species: Dogs, cats and birds. Wild animals and birds of prey not allowed.
cards.carrier: Required: a separate carrying container that keeps the pet out of sight. Pet under 10 kg (22 lb); container no more than 100 cm combined (example: 45 × 30 × 25 cm). Pet and carrier must not take a seat or block the aisle.
cards.fee: No pet fee stated for a carrier on your lap or at your feet. If you want a seat for the pet, you pay an adult fare.
cards.booking: No pet booking needed; just your own ticket (plus an adult ticket if the pet gets a seat).
cards.rules: All pets must be vaccinated (Korail names rabies). Under Korean rail law, a pet without these safety measures that harms other passengers can get you removed from the train or fined up to KRW 500,000 (approx. US$377).
cards.service: Not stated on Korail's pet page. Korean law bars refusing a disabled person's assistance dog that wears the official assistance-dog mark (see the Taxis card).
cards.tourist: Korail has an English booking site and an English call center: +82 1599-7777 (8 am–8 pm Korea time). Whether your US card works on the site: not stated; confirm with Korail.

cards.sub: SR's trains from Suseo (southeast Seoul) to Busan, Mokpo and more
cards.species: Small pets such as dogs and cats. Fighting-dog breeds (SR names Tosa, Doberman, Shepherd and Pit bull), birds of prey, rodents, reptiles, poultry and livestock not allowed.
cards.carrier: Required. Pet under 60 cm long; pet plus carrier no more than 10 kg (22 lb). It travels as carry-on and must not take a seat or block the aisle.
cards.booking: You cannot book a seat for a pet on SRT. No separate pet ticket is mentioned.
cards.rules: Pets need their vaccinations, including rabies.
cards.service: Assistance dogs for people with visual, hearing or physical disabilities may ride without a carrier.
cards.tourist: SRT sells tickets on its own website and app. English booking and foreign cards: not stated in SR's pet notice; confirm with SR.

cards.sub: Seoul Metro, Lines 1–8 (other cities and lines have their own terms)
cards.species: Small pets. Seoul Metro's terms also allow a small number of birds or insects.
cards.carrier: Required: a dedicated carrier that keeps the pet out of sight and stops any unpleasant smell. No size or weight limit given.
cards.fee: No fare for the pet; you pay your own fare (from KRW 1,550 with a transit card, approx. US$1.17).
cards.rules: Staff can refuse boarding or remove you if the rules aren't met. Seoul Metro's terms also list a KRW 10,000 (approx. US$8) surcharge per item for carrying a non-hazardous prohibited item.
cards.service: Allowed: assistance dogs that wear the assistance-dog mark.
cards.tourist: No pet paperwork. Pay with a T-money card or a single-journey ticket from the station machines.
cards.link_text: Seoul Metro terms of carriage, Art. 35 (Korean)

cards.sub: City buses, express (Kobus-type) and intercity buses
cards.species: Small pets in a carrier. Busan Central Bus Terminal also lists fighting-dog breeds, birds of prey, rodents and reptiles as not allowed.
cards.carrier: Required. Each bus company sets weight and size limits. Example: for express buses at Busan Central Bus Terminal, the carrier must be under 50 × 40 × 20 cm and pet plus carrier no more than 10 kg (22 lb).
cards.fee: No pet fee stated. At Busan Central Bus Terminal you can buy the seat next to you for the pet (one adult ticket).
cards.booking: Ask the bus company before you travel; rules vary by company.
cards.rules: Keep the pet in the carrier on the platform and on the bus. Busan's terminal says you can be refused if other passengers complain.
cards.service: Assistance dogs are accepted (Busan Central Bus Terminal; Korean law also protects marked assistance dogs).
cards.tourist: Rules are posted in Korean only. Show the carrier at the ticket counter or to the driver before you board.

cards.carrier: Expected: Korea's tourism board (VisitKorea) says your pet should be in a carrier and that rules vary by company. No size limit given.
cards.fee: No pet fee stated; drivers can refuse.
cards.booking: None; ask the driver before you get in.
cards.rules: Korean law leaves pets in taxis to each operator's terms of carriage.
cards.service: A disabled person with an assistance dog that wears the official mark can't be refused without a lawful reason; the fine is up to KRW 3,000,000 (approx. US$2,264).
cards.tourist: A carrier makes a yes much more likely. If you need a guaranteed ride, book a pet taxi (next card).
cards.link_text: Easy Law: pets on public transport (Korean)

cards.species: Pets (species not stated). Up to 3 people and 3 pets per ride.
cards.fee: One-way fare set by start and end point, shown in the app before you book; or hourly hire (minimum 1 hour). Cancellation: 10% from 24 to 9 hours before (max KRW 8,000), 50% from 9 to 1 hour before (max KRW 8,000), 100% within 1 hour (max KRW 15,000, approx. US$11), no-show 100% (max KRW 30,000, approx. US$23).
cards.booking: In the Kakao T app under 펫 (Pet), from 2 weeks to 30 minutes ahead; no phone booking. If no driver accepts, the booking fails.
cards.rules: Rides must start in Seoul, Incheon, Gyeonggi, Daejeon, Sejong, Chungcheong (North and South), Daegu, Gyeongbuk, Busan, Ulsan or Gyeongnam. Jeju, Gangwon and Jeolla are not listed. Kakao says drivers are licensed for animal transport, pet injury insurance is included, and cleaning fees are covered.
cards.tourist: The pet service is in the Korean Kakao T app. Kakao says Visa, Mastercard, JCB and AMEX cards issued abroad work for pet rides. Signing up with a US phone number: not stated; confirm. Kakao's English app for visitors (k.ride) doesn't mention pets.

cards.sub: Cabin rules on Korean airlines' domestic flights
cards.species: Dogs, cats and birds on Asiana, Jeju Air and Trinity Airways (formerly T'way); Jeju Air and Trinity require pets at least 8 weeks old, Asiana at least 16 weeks. Asiana and Trinity ban dangerous or fighting breeds.
cards.carrier: Asiana: pet plus carrier no more than 7 kg (15 lb) in the cabin, carrier up to 45 × 32 × 21 cm. Jeju Air: no more than 9 kg (20 lb), carrier up to 100 cm combined (width 37, height 23 cm). Trinity: no more than 9 kg, hard carrier width 37, height 23 cm, combined 115 cm. Korean Air: 7 kg in the cabin (2019 Korean Air newsroom figure; confirm).
cards.fee: Asiana: KRW 30,000 (approx. US$23) up to 32 kg, KRW 60,000 (approx. US$45) for 32–45 kg in the hold. Jeju Air: KRW 25,000 (approx. US$19) per flight, cabin only. Trinity: KRW 30,000 (approx. US$23), paid at the airport, cabin only. Korean Air and Jin Air: confirm with airline.
cards.booking: Required. Asiana: at least 24 hours (business days) ahead through its reservation center (US 1-800-227-4262). Jeju Air: on its website or app, or call 1599-1500. Trinity: online up to 1 day before, by phone up to 2½ hours before.
cards.rules: 1 pet per adult; Jeju Air and Trinity cap it at 6 pets per flight. Jeju Air and Trinity: check in at the counter, no online check-in. Asiana: children can't take a pet in the cabin; no sedated or pregnant pets; no snub-nosed pets in the hold.
cards.service: Asiana: service dogs with an ID tag or harness ride at your feet. Other airlines: confirm.
cards.tourist: Book the pet when you book your seat, then check in at the counter with the carrier. Asiana sells carriers at Gimpo and Jeju airports (KRW 45,000, approx. US$34).

cards.sub: Mokpo ↔ Jeju (Queen Jenuvia II, Queen Mary) and Jindo ↔ Jeju (Santa Monica)
cards.carrier: Required: a dedicated soft or hard carrier, or boarding may be refused. Medium and large dogs also need a muzzle and a leash or harness, and you still bring a carrier.
cards.fee: Pets only in pet rooms or seats. The operator's FAQ lists Pet Suite (private, up to 4 people) at KRW 268,000 weekdays / 294,200 weekends (approx. US$202 / US$222), and Pet Standard (pets under 10 kg, sold as a 2-bed set) at KRW 124,000 / 136,000 (approx. US$94 / US$103). Fares vary; confirm at booking.
cards.booking: Book a pet room or seat with your ticket. Pet-conomy: pets under 4 kg, 1 per person. On the Santa Monica, pet premium and business seats have no weight limit, but the pet stays in its carrier.
cards.rules: Outside pet areas the pet must stay in its carrier; restaurants may be off-limits. A free "pet passport" with stamps is optional (apply 7 days before) and is not a ticket.

cards.sub: Wando ↔ Jeju (Silver Cloud and other ships)
cards.species: Dogs, cats, rabbits, birds, reptiles, rodents and more. Animals other than dogs and cats must be in an escape-proof carrier. Dangerous breeds, aggressive or venomous animals may be refused.
cards.carrier: Required: a carrier your pet fits in completely, for boarding, leaving the ship and moving around. Medium and large dogs may walk with a muzzle and leash, but you must still bring a carrier.
cards.fee: Pet room price shown at booking; confirm. One pet-room ticket = 1 passenger + 1 pet.
cards.booking: Pets travel only in the Pet Room (shared, 18 or 35 people) or Special Pet Room (private, 4 or 6 people). Book online, by phone (1688-2100) or at the terminal.
cards.rules: 1 pet per passenger; no pets in regular cabins, the lobby or restaurants. Using a regular cabin can mean a room change and extra charges. A pet that stays in your car on the car deck needs no pet room, but you can't visit it while sailing; tell staff and arrive 1 hour before departure.
cards.service: Not stated on the pet rules; Hanil has a separate disability service page. Confirm with Hanil.
cards.tourist: Korean-language site; booking asks for name, sex, date of birth and phone. Hanil sells carriers, muzzles and leashes at its offices.
cards.link_text: Hanil Express: FAQ and pet rules (Korean)

cards.sub: Your own or a rental car
cards.carrier: Recommended. Korean law bans driving with a pet in your arms or on your lap.
cards.fee: Fine for driving with a pet in your arms: up to KRW 200,000 (approx. US$151); on-the-spot penalty KRW 40,000 (approx. US$30) for cars, KRW 50,000 (approx. US$38) for vans. Rental pet fees: confirm with rental company.
cards.booking: Ask the rental company whether pets are allowed; rules vary by company.
cards.rules: Pets of 20 kg (44 lb) or more may ride with their owner in a van-type cargo vehicle (a pet-moving service), an option when public transport won't take them.
cards.tourist: Car ferries to Jeju carry cars; Hanil allows a pet to stay in your car on the car deck (see above).
cards.link_text: Easy Law: pets on public transport (Korean)

intro: Most Korean hotels that take pets have only a few dedicated pet rooms or a pet package, and many accept only small dogs. Book the pet room or package directly with the hotel, well ahead of time: some take pet bookings by phone only, and several hotels with pet rooms are listed as “no pets” on booking sites.

Bring your pet’s rabies vaccination certificate dated within the last year (the same records you use for entry). Expect a carrier or stroller in public areas, no pets in restaurants, pools or spas, and a rule against leaving your pet alone in the room. Some hotels ban the breeds Korea classes as dangerous (Tosa, American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Rottweiler and their mixes).

hotels.name: Four Seasons Hotel Seoul
hotels.species: Pets (species not stated; cats: confirm with hotel)
hotels.fee: KRW 250,000 per room, tax and service included (approx. US$189)
hotels.conditions: Pets must be fully vaccinated; you sign a consent form. Cart or carrier outside the room, leash in public areas; no restaurants, spa or pool. Don’t leave your pet alone (the concierge can arrange a pet sitter in advance). Book by contacting the hotel: +82 2 6388 5000.

hotels.name: Vista Walkerhill Seoul
hotels.fee: “Oh My Pet” package from KRW 589,000 per night (approx. US$445) for 2 people + 1 pet; no separate pet fee stated
hotels.conditions: Documents: not stated, confirm with hotel. Carrier in public areas; no restaurants or bars; bring your own pet food. Whether pets may be left alone: confirm with hotel. Book the package (VISTA Pet Concept Room; phone booking available). The neighboring Grand Walkerhill does not take pets.

hotels.name: Mondrian Seoul Itaewon
hotels.weight: 13 kg (29 lb) max for two dogs (combined or each: confirm with hotel)
hotels.fee: KRW 100,000 cleaning fee (approx. US$75); per stay or per night: confirm with hotel
hotels.conditions: Documents and public-area rules are not stated on the official page: confirm with hotel. Book the Pet-Stay offer.

hotels.name: Hotel Cappuccino
hotels.weight: Under 15 kg (33 lb) and under 40 cm tall
hotels.pets: 2 (extra charge for the 2nd dog; amount: confirm with hotel)
hotels.fee: Bark Room rate; no separate pet fee stated. US$250 charge for soiled linens or a mess in the corridor
hotels.conditions: Rabies certificate dated within 1 year plus vaccination copies, and pet registration by QR code; without them the stay is refused with no refund. Dog carried or in a carrier in the hotel; never left alone in the room; Korean dangerous breeds banned. Book a Bark Room.

hotels.name: Grand Josun Busan
hotels.fee: “Meongcance” pet package: the hotel site showed KRW 1,320,000 per night (approx. US$996) tax included, but 2026 press quoted from KRW 770,000 (approx. US$581): confirm with hotel. Includes a KRW 55,000/night cleaning fee; 2nd dog KRW 100,000 + tax (approx. US$75)
hotels.conditions: You sign a rules agreement at check-in; vaccination proof: confirm with hotel. Cage or stroller when moving through the hotel; dogs only in the lobby, elevators and room; dangerous dogs may be refused. Phone booking only (+82 51 922 5000); say how many dogs when you book.

hotels.name: Ananti at Busan Cove
hotels.fee: Pet-room rate; no separate pet fee stated
hotels.conditions: Documents: not stated, confirm with hotel. No dogs in restaurants or other facilities outside the room. Book the pet room by phone (1877-5707) about 3 weeks before check-in; it can sell out. An undeclared dog means a cleaning charge and you may be asked to leave.

hotels.name: Sunset Hotel
hotels.fee: KRW 30,000 per pet per night (approx. US$23)
hotels.conditions: Proof of rabies vaccination. Never leave your pet alone in the room; diaper (manner belt) required. Pet stays only in Deluxe Family, Family Queen Twin or Superior Suite rooms. Ask the hotel and reserve in advance: +82 51 730 9900.

hotels.name: Somerset Jeju Shinhwa World
hotels.weight: Under 10 kg (22 lb) (the rules PDF says up to 10 kg: confirm with hotel)
hotels.fee: Pet-room rate; 2nd dog KRW 55,000 per stay (approx. US$42); KRW 300,000 refundable deposit (approx. US$226)
hotels.conditions: Rabies certificate dated within 1 year required at check-in; dogs fully vaccinated and at least 3 months old. Stroller or cage inside buildings; no pool, sauna or restaurant; Korean dangerous breeds and mixes banned. Whether dogs may be left alone: confirm with hotel. Book the Pet Friendly Room (reservations@shinhwaworld.com).

hotels.name: The Best Jeju Seongsan Hotel
hotels.fee: Pet-room rate; no separate pet fee stated
hotels.conditions: Rabies and combination vaccines within the last year: bring the certificate. Carrier, stroller or carried in the lobby, corridors and elevators; no restaurants, cafés or pool; never leave your dog alone. Book a Pet Double or Pet Family Twin room on the official site: +82 64 784 0550.
